newsitem.title: USA: Kerr-McGee expects benefit from pigment hike.
newsitem.headline: Kerr-McGee expects benefit from pigment hike.

text.p: Kerr-McGee Corp said Tuesday it expects to realize the benefits of a recently announced pigment price increase in the second quarter.
The company did not say how much the increase would impact its earnings.
Earlier in the day, Kerr-McGee said it earned $70 million, or $1.45 per common share, for the first quarter, compared with $48 million, or 94 cents, in the year-ago period.

The company said its earnings in the quarter were helped by strong crude and natural gas prices. Lower coal prices and higher costs for its Galatia mine in Illinois offset some of those gains, however.

On Monday, the company said operations in one part of the Galatia mine was suspended last Tuesday because of elevated levels of carbon monoxide but believes production at Galatia this year could be hurt by as much as one million tons from the suspension.
The company also said its chemical profit was off because of lower titanium dioxide prices and higher production costs.
